newsitem.title: UK: UK to take action to ban RPM on OTC medicines.
newsitem.headline: UK to take action to ban RPM on OTC medicines.

text.p: The UK's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) said on Friday it would take legal action to remove resale price maintenance (RPM) on over-the-counter medicines, a spokesman at the OFT said.
RPM is the process by which retail prices of branded over-the-counter medicines such as painkillers and indigestion treatments are fixed at point of sale.
OFT head John Bridgeman said in a statement: "There are good reasons for believing that it is time to end price-fixing on branded antiseptics, painkillers and vitamin pills."
The move follows a campaign in which supermarket group ASDA Plc has faced court injunctions for cutting prices of branded medicines and removed some products from its shelves in protest.
ASDA has maintained that prices charged under RPM are too expensive and has consistently priced its own-brand comparable goods at lower prices.
Supporters of RPM claim abolishing the system will threaten thousands of small pharmacies in rural areas which may not be able to survive in the face of cut-price competition from supermarkets.
